neighbours.label: the start of an adverse outcome phrase after a causal verb (lead to a ..., cause an ..., lull into a ...): anticipating a harmful consequence
fire: Ignoring the leak for months can result in a collapse of the ceiling.
Too much screen time may contribute to a decline in reading skills.
The new tariffs could trigger a wave of layoffs across the region.
Sleeping only four hours a night often leads to a weakened immune system.
Constant criticism can push children into a deep sense of failure.
Overfishing has caused a sharp fall in cod stocks.
Mixing these two drugs may produce an irregular heartbeat.
Skipping maintenance eventually leads to an expensive breakdown.
quiet: Fixing the leak promptly can result in a much drier ceiling.
Daily reading may contribute to a rise in vocabulary.
The new park could attract a wave of tourists across the region.
Sleeping eight hours a night often leads to a stronger immune system.
Warm praise can push children into a lasting love of learning.
The festival has drawn a large crowd every summer.
The bakery sells an excellent rye loaf.
Regular maintenance eventually leads to a smoother ride.

predictions: causal verb + harmful outcome 0.3-0.65 on the article; same verbs with beneficial outcomes and non-causal sentences low
notes: Card: peaks on ' a'/' an'/',' opening negative consequences (fear of abandonment, increase in the urge, lack of statistical data); promotes ' false' ' flawed' ' misunderstanding'. Probe: 'lulled investors into a false sense' 0.641, 'lead to a drop in energy' 0.410, 'and a lack of funding' 0.339, 'cause an increase in blood pressure' 0.306; 'lead to a boost in mood' 0.142, recipe 0.006.
